src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:73-96 `_called_names` returns {text, text.lower(), ascii_lower} per call-position token; `_refuse_database_routines` (192-205) compares `LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) IN (names)`. Folding server: stored function `ETAT` with accent (ROUTINE_NAME 'ÉTAT') -> LOWER = 'état'; a call written `ÉTAT(x)` or `état(x)` yields 'état' via text.lower(), so it matches. Non-folding server (LOWER only folds ASCII): LOWER('ÉTAT') = 'État'. Call written `ÉTAT(x)`: candidates 'ÉTAT','état','État' -> 'État' (ascii_lower) matches. Call written `état(x)` (MySQL/MariaDB resolves routine names case-insensitively, so this still calls ÉTAT): candidates for 'état' are all the single string 'état' (written, lower and ascii-lower coincide), which does not equal 'État' -> no match, the routine is not refused. Same for a defined 'État' called as `état(x)`. So the docstring's claim (lines 79-81) that the three variants make a lookup match 'whether or not the server folds non-ASCII letters' is false: on a non-folding server a call whose non-ASCII letter case differs from the defined name's is missed. Only the written-case and the all-folded cases are covered; the mixed-case mismatch is not. On a server that folds (the usual MySQL case) the code behaves correctly. The claim is source-authored, so a counterexample in the authored docstring suffices; the failing input is reachable by a client query, but the non-folding-server precondition is hypothetical, so severity is limited.
